Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My girlfriend is moving to a different country. I feel like she will ditch me for someone better. Should I break up with her?
Answer: To determine if what I am doing is the right life strategy, I multiply it. What happens if I repeatedly leave people before they can leave me? I never let down my guard. I never know intimacy. I never trust, and cannot be trusted. I never learn how to express what I want, how to have a difficult conversation, how to create sturdy relationships. I end up isolated, lonely, in pain. The very pain I was sure I was avoiding by leaving first. Conclusion: this is not the right life strategy. It’s maladaptive, ensures I miss everything that is beautiful, ensures I cause the very things I fear. What happens if instead I communicate clearly, love with my whole heart, remind myself pain cannot be avoided, so I might as well give myself fully? I definitely suffer from heartbreak. I can’t escape this. But also, I live with courage, know intimacy, create relationships that are real and deep. Each relationship teaches me about relationships so that I get better at life’s most important skill. And, I improve the relationship with myself: instead of being someone who robs me, who sabotages me, I become someone I can count on - and someone I am certain is worth loving.

Question: Why don't people mind their own business? How do you politely let them know that you want to be left alone?
Answer: I am fully responsible for this but thank you for your effort. Thank you so much for your concern, but I’ve got this. I have this covered but thank you for asking. I appreciate you, and don’t need any help for this. I would much rather handle this on my own but thank you! I actually am not looking for anyone’s support on this but thank you. To me this is a private matter but thank you. I actually want to be left alone - thank you for respecting my boundaries.

Question: What did you do to your hair that you will never do again?
Answer: I’ve never done anything to my hair: I’ve never straightened it, colored it, permed it or done anything to it other than have someone cut it. Except. There was a very unfortunate episode where a friend convinced me to highlight it. I hated everything about it: the feeling of being closely assessed, the sense that there was something wrong about the natural color of my hair (ugh this is so…flat!), the yanking, the smell of chemicals and the result. It just didn’t work for me. It took a long time to grow out. Since that time, I let my hair do whatever she wants: curl, puff, bounce, become grey. You do you, hair. I like you no matter what.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Why do people say that "relationships take work"?
Answer: Because dreaming of a fairy tale wedding is easy, and becoming a stronger couple when things get hard takes work. Because pretending everything is “fine” is easy and putting love, energy and time into understanding each other takes work. Because, feeling like “he should just know” is easy, and learning how to ask for what I want takes work. Because white lies are easy and telling the truth takes work. Because being aloof and dismissive is easy and making sure you are a safe person even when you are angry takes work. Because giving up when things get rocky is easy and learning how to communicate is work. Because staying angry is easy and forgiving takes work. Because blame is easy and taking responsibility is work. Because saying yes to everything and then feeling resentful is easy and good boundaries take work. Because thinking only of what works for me is easy and being a team is work. Because looking for someone to “make me happy” and “complete me” is easy and working on myself takes work. Constant work. The best work.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What do you wish someone had told you about relationships in high school?
Answer: What I remember most about High School is the energy I expended to get others to like me, in particular if they seemed aloof or if they acted in a way that was not consistent. Inconsistency felt like such a rush. I can make you love me. I wish someone had told me that any form of chasing is ineffective. It doesn’t work but when it does you end up surrounded by people who are not really interested in you. I wish someone had said “be who you are and communicate as clearly as you can, and refrain from expending effort in influencing how others feel about you.” You are not supposed to “win people over.” Any form of a chase, any effort, any plot, any plan to “get someone to like me” will accomplish the opposite of what I want to find: someone as interested in me as I am in them.
